subject: Re: Astrava evaluation: cost playbook & close timeline
body:
From: Connor O’Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@astrava.com>, Ben Thompson <ben.thompson@astrava.com>
Cc: 
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 14:05:00 -0500
Subject: Astrava evaluation: cost playbook & next steps

Hi Elena / Ben,

Thanks again for the time today. As promised, attached is a first-pass mutual action plan and a lightweight cost playbook that maps your expected evaluation traffic to token-level unit economics. The MAP has the milestones we discussed (POC, privacy review, procurement, pilot). The cost sheet contains two scenarios (pilot light / pilot heavy) and the assumptions we used.

Quick summary:
- Pilot target: 50k user sessions over 30 days (avg 120 tokens prompt, 450 tokens response)
- Baseline token rate used: $0.0009 / 1k tokens for model variant A (open-model quantized path)
- Cache assumptions: 12% prefix cache hit; KV cache reduces repeated context by ~8% on average
- Batching: continuous batching with effective batch size 6 in peak windows, 1-2 in tail windows
- Expected blended tokens/$: ~1,250 tokens per dollar (pilot light) -> ~1,650 tokens per dollar (pilot heavy, more batching + cache)

What I need from you to finalize the MAP:
1) Confirmation on expected average session length (do you expect longer multi-turn flows?)
2) Any compliance artifacts required during pilot (SOC2 checklist items already in the MAP)
3) Procurement timeline / preferred PO contact (we listed Ben as procurement lead; confirm)

Attached: astrava_map_v1.xlsx (MAP + cost workbook).

Planned next steps (proposed):
- Your sign-off on scope + evaluation criteria (by Fri 11/13)
- Redwood to deliver a token-econ sensitivity table and a recommended runtime config (by Mon 11/16)
- Pilot start target: week of 11/23 (pending PO)

If you want, I can loop in Stephanie (SE) and Sean (finance) for a short call to walk through the token rows and caching/batching tradeoffs.

Cheers,
Connor
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
---

On Wed, 11 Nov 2026 at 09:18 AM Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@astrava.com> wrote:
> From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@astrava.com>

>
> Thanks, Connor 94 this is a great start. A couple of clarifying questions before we sign the MAP: 
>
> 1) Token per call assumptions: are the prompt/response numbers per user session or per API call? We have both short single-turn searches and longer assistant flows; we need to price both.
> 2) Batching: you mention an "effective batch size 6" 94 how sensitive is cost to batch size in our load shape? We will have spiky traffic at 2x daily peak.
> 3) Caching: what do you define as prefix cache hit? Is that on the customer side (we should dedupe) or runtime-level prefix caching? Are there limits for privacy?
>
> Also, procurement asked for a simple 30/60/90 estimated spend table and an explanation of the variance drivers.
>
> Can we get a follow-up that disaggregates tokens/$ by model variant and shows sensitivity to cache hit rate (+/- 10%) and batch sizes of 1 / 4 / 8 / 16?
>
> Best,
>Elena
Dir. Product Operations | Astrava Health

On Thu, 11 Nov 2026 at 15:04:00 -0500 Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com> wrote:
> From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
> To: Connor O’Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
> Date: Thu, 11 Nov 2026 15:04:00 -0500
> Subject: RE: Fwd: Astrava evaluation: cost playbook & next steps
>
> Connor / team,
>
> Attached is a compact assumptions doc and the sensitivity matrix you asked for (token_econ_assumptions.pdf). High level points:
>
> - Model variants: we priced three paths:
>   * Variant A (quantized open model): baseline $0.0009 / 1k tokens; good latency; best cost with quantization and batching.
>   * Variant B (opt-compat medium): $0.0025 / 1k tokens; higher quality for long-context flows.
>   * Variant C (fallback managed): $0.0060 / 1k tokens; used for high-SLA/low-latency small requests.
>
> - Batching sensitivity (peak shape):
>   * Batch 1: baseline throughput, tokens/$ ~1,100 (no batching)
>   * Batch 4: tokens/$ ~1,300
>   * Batch 8: tokens/$ ~1,550
>   * Batch 16: tokens/$ ~1,720
>   Note: batching benefits taper; large batches increase tail latency for single-turn flows.
>
> - Caching assumptions:
>   * Prefix cache hit is runtime-level prefix matching of identical prompts or canonicalized templates (we _do_ not persist customer prompts outside the runtime; customer data stays in your VPC/pilot workspace).
>   * Privacy constraints can disable prefix caching; KV cache (context reuse across turns) is safe for pilot and reduces repeated token decode by ~6-12% depending on dialog shape.
>   * Sensitivity table attached shows tokens/$ at cache hit rates [0%, 5%, 10%, 20%]. Example: moving from 0%->10% cache hit improves tokens/$ by ~8-12% depending on model variant and batch size.
>
> - 30/60/90 estimated spend (pilot light / pilot heavy):
>   * Pilot light (mostly short searches): $9k / $22k / $45k
>   * Pilot heavy (mix with long assistant flows): $18k / $45k / $95k
>   Drivers: avg tokens per session, % long flows, average batch size during peaks, cache hit rate.
>
> Attachments: token_econ_assumptions.pdf (sensitivity matrices + example calc), astrava_map_v1_responses.xlsx (populated per-variant rows).
>
> Proposed immediate deliverable for Astrava: a short two-page summary that shows (a) recommended runtime config per workload segment, (b) best- and worst-case 30/60/90 spend with driver callouts, and (c) an acceptance criteria checklist for the pilot (latency SLOs, quality eval pass rates). I can produce that by EOD Fri 11/13 if Connor confirms.
>
> -Steph
>

>

>

>
> Cheers,
>Connor
